display: Bambu PAHT-CF (high-temp carbon-fibre nylon) — dual_pdm / four-bolt adaptor
notes: RAFTLESS RECIPE VALIDATED 2026-09-02/03 -- SCOPE: LOW-CONTACT-AREA PARTS ONLY (user, 2026-09-05). The validation parts (dual_pdm cases left+right, 2/2, ~18.6mm tall) touch the bed with a thin wall-perimeter outline + tree-support first layers + brim -- almost no continuous solid area, so almost no accumulated first-layer shrinkage stress. A SOLID PLATE (e.g. the four_bolt_adaptor, ~107x85 slab, 100% infill) is a very very different regime -- the classic PA warp worst case -- and remains UNVALIDATED raftless; the PETG raft route below is still the proven method for that geometry class. Raftless recipe where it applies: direct on Textured PEI, 290C, bed 100C constant (profile default, no ramp), FIRST_SPEED_SCALE=0.5, LAYER_TIME=120, BRIM=20 BRIM_INNER=1 (fused, gap 0), tree supports organic/plate-only/15deg where roofs need them, chamber soaked (bed 100C hold >=15min, ~40C chamber proxy). Zero lift; tall-part Z-gradient concern did not materialise. OLDER RAFT ROUTE (2026-08-26, four_bolt_adaptor v6, large flat plate): print on a 1.2mm solid Overture-PETG raft via slice/splice_raft.py (dissimilar-material raft, per community practice for PAHT-CF) — raft runs the full Overture recipe (its soak/ramp/brim), M400 U1 swap pause, then this profile at 290C over the 70C bed, 100% infill, chamber pre-warmed (bed 100C hold, nozzle-proxy ~40C). Zero warp/lift; the PA/PETG interface peels clean. Known issue: top-surface POROSITY + fuzz. Spool was dried to 15% RH (user-reported, 2026-08-26) before this print — BORDERLINE for PA (want <=10%): starting moisture is the prime suspect, in-print reabsorption (spool exposed through pre-warm + raft phase) secondary, top-layer speed third. Candidates in order: dry harder (<=10%, 65-70C, longer), keep spool bagged until the swap pause, slow top_surface_speed, +1-2% top-layer flow. Hard requirements: hardened nozzle (installed); dry filament; door closed. Tall parts (dual_pdm enclosure) NOT yet validated — expect the Z-gradient effects a 4mm plate avoided. Distinct from pa-cf-bambu.json. No 0.6 entry — verify the Orca 0.6 profile name before adding. RAFT-PRINT BRIM RULE (learned 2026-08-27, dual_pdm enclosure): the PART slice must NOT use brim_type=auto_brim — auto mode ignores brim_width and scaled to ~13mm on a 20mm-tall part, overrunning the 4mm raft margin by ~8mm/side (loops printed in air off the raft edge; sacrificial, but sloppy). Set brim_type=outer_only with brim_width <= the raft margin, or grow the raft MARGIN to match the intended brim.
